extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer reviewers, and authors (medical journals)
extracted.subtask_description: ICMJE guidance on the ethical and procedural responsibilities of journals, editors, and reviewers in the manuscript submission and peer‑review process for medical journals. Covers conflict disclosure, confidentiality, timeliness, and editorial authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal responsibility for reviewer selection systems
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the responsibility of the journal to ensure that systems are in place for selection of appropriate reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals must maintain processes and infrastructure to identify and select suitably qualified, unbiased reviewers for submitted manuscripts. This is an institutional/journal-level duty rather than only an individual editor task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer access to all relevant materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers have access to all materials that may be relevant to the evaluation of the manuscript, including supplementary material for e-only publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should provide reviewers with the manuscript plus any supplementary files, data, appendices, or online-only material necessary to make a thorough assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret reviewer comments in context of declared relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer comments are properly assessed and interpreted in the context of their declared relationships and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should weigh reviews with awareness of reviewers' declared conflicts or relationships and interpret critiques accordingly; declaration does not automatically invalidate a review but must inform editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial discretion on peer review and content selection
rubrics_metrics.description: A peer-reviewed journal is under no obligation to send submitted manuscripts for review, and under no obligation to follow reviewer recommendations, favorable or negative. The editor of a journal is ultimately responsible for the selection of all its content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors retain final responsibility and may decide not to send submissions for external review; reviewer advice is advisory and not binding. Editorial decisions should be defensible and based on journal scope, quality, and ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of relationships and activities that might bias evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should declare their relationships and activities that might bias their evaluation of a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At invitation and during review, reviewers must disclose financial, personal, professional, or other relationships/activities that could affect impartiality. Declarations should be sufficient for editors to assess potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recusal from review when a conflict exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Recuse themselves from the peer-review process if a conflict exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer has a conflict of interest (financial, personal, competitive, etc.) that could compromise objectivity, they should decline the review. If uncertain, disclose to the editor and seek guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose to editors any relationships that could bias opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose to editors any relationships or activities that could bias their opinions of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond initial declaration, reviewers must proactively inform editors of any relevant relationships discovered or arising during the review that might influence their judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask invitees about relationships/activities that could complicate review
rubrics_metrics.description: Be asked at the time they are asked to critique a manuscript if they have relationships or activities that could complicate their review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should ask potential reviewers at invitation whether any relationships or activities (e.g., collaborations, institutional ties, financial interests) might complicate their ability to provide an unbiased review; invitees should answer honestly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of submitted manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts submitted to journals are privileged communications that are authors' private, confidential property. Reviewers should respect the privileged nature of the manuscripts they are entrusted with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must not share, distribute, cite, or use information from manuscripts under review except with explicit permission from the editor. Confidentiality extends to supplementary materials and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive, timely, fair, and unbiased review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should be conducted in a constructive manner, with reviewers providing timely, fair, and unbiased reviews that help authors improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should focus on improving the manuscript, identify strengths and weaknesses, avoid ad hominem or insulting language, be fair and evidence‑based, and be submitted within agreed timelines or declined promptly if unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use submitted materials to advance own work or disadvantage authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not attempt to use the materials to advance their own work or to disadvantage the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must not appropriate ideas, data, or plans from manuscripts for their own research, nor take actions intended to delay or block competitors' publication. Suspected appropriation should be reported to editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not contact authors directly
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not contact the authors directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All communication between reviewers and authors should be mediated by the journal/editorial office to preserve confidentiality, manage conflicts, and avoid undue influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report suspected misconduct to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should report suspected misconduct to the editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer suspects plagiarism, data fabrication/falsification, unethical research practices, undisclosed conflicts, or other misconduct, they should notify the editor with evidence or rationale rather than acting unilaterally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and adoption of ICMJE Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: ICMJE Recommendations are widely adopted by medical journals worldwide and serve as the foundational standard for ethical conduct in scholarly publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals, editors, reviewers, and authors should be aware that these recommendations represent broadly accepted norms and may be used by journals to shape policies and editorial decisions.
